messages.author: 55bf66bb7cca8b78
messages.subject: Unweighted Least Squares
parts:
Hi,

While running various ordinal CFA models I noticed that the p-values were specified as "(unknown)" and "NA" when ULS was used. I have searched through the postings and noticed it was mentioned that ULS is not distributed as a chi-square asymptotically and was wondering if that was the reason for no p-value calculated or if there is some other reason.

Also, I have seen various references that robust estimation methods like ULSMV are appropriate for continuous variables, but are they appropriate for ordinal variables? I ask because mainly because I am surprised that my models are showing worse fit if I specify the variables as ordinal and use a robust method like ULSMV versus if I use ULS. This is surprising because my sample size is large (n=1236) and my items are univariate normal, though not multivariate normal.

Thanks.

John

messages.subject: Re: Unweighted Least Squares
parts:
On 06/25/2013 09:14 AM, John Taylor wrote:
> Hi,
>
> While running various ordinal CFA models I noticed that the p-values
> were specified as "(unknown)" and "NA" when ULS was used. I have
> searched through the postings and noticed it was mentioned that ULS is
> not distributed as a chi-square asymptotically and was wondering if that
> was the reason for no p-value calculated or if there is some other reason.

That is the reason indeed. We try to 'avoid' that users report
(unscaled) chi-square test statistics in their papers if estimator="ULS".

> Also, I have seen various references that robust estimation methods like
> ULSMV are appropriate for continuous variables, but are they appropriate
> for ordinal variables? I ask because mainly because I am surprised that
> my models are showing worse fit if I specify the variables as ordinal
> and use a robust method like ULSMV versus if I use ULS. This is
> surprising because my sample size is large (n=1236) and my items are
> univariate normal, though not multivariate normal.

That is an interesting observation. I looked for papers/sources that
could shed some light on this but could not find anything.

Anyone else?

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: Unweighted Least Squares
parts:
Hi everyone,

I know this was quite an old topic. I came across this topic, when I was trying to understand how to interpret an (unknown) and "NA"  chi-square p-value. I was also running an ordinal CFA model with the ULS estimator for 51 Likert-scale items responded on a 5-point scale, which with 11 subscales. The sample size a bit small, N=240. All the other indexes that I am checking seems fine to me,  χ² (1169) =1653.35, p = NA, CFI= 0.98, TLI= 0.98, RMSEA= 0.04, SRMR= 0.07, with significant factor loadings-standardized values ranging from 0.54 to 1.00.

Should I report it as I did above or just mention that "It is recommended to 'avoid' reporting (unscaled) chi-square test statistics in results of a CFA, if the "ULS" was used as an estimator." and not mention about it? Should I refer to this discussion group as a reference or anyone knows/has a paper on this?


Thanks,

Almer
